articles.title: Carrie Coon & Lily James Humanized Cult Member And Leader In Guy Nattiv’s ‘The Liberation’ – Contenders L.A.
articles.content: Carrie Coon and Lily James grew to understand their roles in the cult thriller The Liberation — compounded by the fact that director Guy Nattiv based the film on his own grandmother. Coon plays Rita, an unhappy woman who finds a place she feels she belongs. Under the mentorship of Ricki King (James), Rita unburdens herself. Eventually, though, Ricki convinces Rita to give her money and divorce her husband. The trio spoke about the film at Deadline’s Contenders Film Los Angeles on Saturday. “I just was so moved by Guy’s grandmother’s story and the way Guy has humanized every step,” Coon said. “We understand just how radical what she’s doing is. As a woman, I understand why she might want to cede all agency to someone else. I understand why a patriarchal structure wasn’t fulfilling to her.” Coon also called The Liberation a love story between Rita and Ricki. Likewise, James did not want to make Ricki a caricature villain. articles.content: Although James Gunn ‘s journey with the Man of Steel has come to a close, Chris Pratt hopes they can take another adventure with Star-Lord soon. The Guardians of the Galaxy star recently confessed he “would love” to make a fourth movie in the MCU franchise with Gunn, following his and Peter Safran’s departure from DC Studios amid David Ellison’s Skydance regime change. “That would be awesome. So, if he wanted to come back and bring it back, man, I would just love that.” Watch on Deadline Earlier this week, Deadline reported that Gunn and Safran were out as co-CEOs and Chairmen of DC Studios after four years, but will continue to produce various DC projects. articles.title: Danny Boyle Talks ‘Ink’, The Common Architecture Of His Movies And More ‘28 Years Later’ As He Receives The Deadline Legend Award
articles.content: Danny Boyle says he used to believe that he that he never made the same film twice, thus a filmography that includes hit movies across genres like Shallow Grave, Trainspotting, 127 Hours, The Beach, 28 Days Later and of course Slumdog Millionaire , the 2009 Best Picture Oscar winner that also won him Best Director. But Boyle, speaking onstage Saturday after receiving the Deadline Legend Award during Deadline’s Contenders Film Los Angeles awards-season event, said he was set straight on that idea long ago. “I can’t remember if it was a press conference or a Q&A in Paris, and this French journalist stood up at the back and said, ‘This is nonsense, Mr. Boyle’,” he recalled. “And I said, ‘Excuse me, what?’ And she said, ‘All your films are exactly the same.’ She said, ‘They’re all about, and it’s usually a guy, who overcomes, who faces insurmountable odds and overcomes them.’ And with that she walked out.” He continued, “Ever since then I’ve accepted that she’s absolutely right — they are all about the same thing, really. And you do realize, and you can see in other filmmakers as well. You’re desperately trying to make a different film, and they basically turn out the same in a way. They’re the skeleton or the the kind of architecture of them is the same somehow. I have to hold my hand up and admit that. So if you keep buying tickets to go and see the films, thank you.” Watch on Deadline Boyle’s latest entry on his list is Ink , based on Hames Graham’s Tony-winning play about Rupert Murdoch and editor Larry Lamb’s efforts to revive the British newspaper The Sun , ushering in a new kind of tabloid journalism with lurid headlines and questionable tactics. Graham adapted the screenplay for the pic, which opened this year’s Venice Film Festival and is gearing for its December 11 release in theaters. articles.title: ‘The Violinist’ Composer Ricky Ho Took Two Months To Write The First Four Notes Of Central Sonata – Contenders L.A.
articles.content: The Violinist is an animated film about a woman searching for her long-lost love after being separated during World War II. She was a violinist, so her music is a major piece of the story. Ricky Ho , one of two composers along with Isabel Latorre, said he toiled over the beginning of the film’s signature piece, “Sunset Sonata.” “It’s not an easy piece to come up with,” Ho said. “It has to be very special, especially the first few notes. Maybe the first two months I write, put aside, take it back, change some notes. In the end, I find these four notes are the perfect notes for the film.” Co-directors Ervin Han and Raúl García joined Ho on the panel at Deadline’s Contenders Film Los Angeles panel Saturday. While the score could be added to the film later, they actually needed to know what notes he was composing as a plot point. Watch on Deadline “We had this back-and-forth because Ricky was composing his music,” García said. “There are scenes where characters write the notes of the sonata.” “Sunset Sonata” connects the leads of the film as their lives drive them apart. Much of the film involves the Japanese occupation of Singapore. “It represents their connection, their love together,” Ho said. “This piece of music is really important throughout the film.” “We are melodrama, and we’re proud of it,” García said. “We need to cry from time to time, and this movie helps you.” Han said he was influenced by the Hong Kong melodramas of the ’80s. He saw them with his parents in theaters and understood their catharsis looking back as an adult. Likewise, Han shared some frustrations with being questioned on animating the film. As a filmmaker, he just thinks of animation as a way to tell certain stories. “Animation has a different contract with the audience,” Han said. “The fact that it’s not real, that it’s drawn, opens up a lot to personal memories, personal life experience, to bring it to the emotion. articles.content: The legendary actress joked with me Sunday night on the red carpet at the Governors Awards in Hollywood that so much of her career has been for her LGBTQ fans. “My career is to create characters for gay Halloween parades,” she said, smiling. articles.content: The Oscar-nominated directors of “ Writing With Fire ,” Rintu Thomas and Sushmit Ghosh, have unveiled the fourth cohort of the Himalayan Story Lab , their year-long fellowship for documentary filmmakers from the South Asian Himalayas. Eight filmmakers will develop six documentaries through the 2026–27 edition, with stories drawn from Kashmir, Ladakh, Uttarakhand, Assam, Manipur, Arunachal Pradesh and Nepal. Cannes Grand Prix winner Payal Kapadia (“All We Imagine as Light”), Sundance winner and Oscar nominee Shaunak Sen (“All That Breathes”), veteran documentarian Sanjay Kak and French editor Yael Bitton are confirmed as mentors. Related Stories 'Adults' Renewed for Season 3 at FX The lab launched in 2023 with just three fellows and has since backed 25 filmmakers from India and Nepal. Thomas and Ghosh, whose “Writing With Fire” won two awards at Sundance, set it up because filmmakers based far from the region’s main production hubs rarely get long-term creative guidance, producing help or a way into the international industry. The model pairs three residential workshops with year-round mentorship on both the creative and producing sides, delivered by documentary directors, producers and editors working in India and overseas. The program isn’t built only around getting individual films to market. Fellows are tracked over a longer stretch of artistic growth, pressed to question their creative approach and coached through the practical demands of making independent documentaries. “Our years of mentoring young filmmakers at Green Hub, a filmmaking initiative in Northeast India, made us aware of a strange asymmetry,” said Thomas. “We began thinking about the invisible distances between talent and opportunity, and whether we could create a space that might collapse those distances.” In “Moving Mountain,” from Lobzang Wangtak and Akshat Jain, a farmer in a deserted village in Ladakh’s Zanskar region tries to revive an ancient glacier canal, and with it his community. It’s been hardly two months since Arcel, in her first-ever leading role in a feature film, was awarded the Volpi Cup for best actress for her breakout performance in “Woman Unknown,” May el-Toukhy ’s riveting, post-World War II drama that was also feted with the festival’s Golden Lion . Praised by Variety ‘s Beatrice Loayza for her “magnetic” performance, Arcel plays a young housemaid whose intimate relationship with a German soldier during World War II threatens her future. Related Stories 'Adults' Renewed for Season 3 at FX Now, on the eve of the closing ceremony of the Thessaloniki Film Festival , which wraps Nov. 15 with el-Toukhy’s Venice winner, Arcel is taking in the news that she’s among the six nominees for best actress at the European Film Awards, whose nominations were announced Saturday afternoon in Thessaloniki. For Arcel, whose grandmother comes from the Greek island of Lesvos, the award ceremony, which will be held in Athens in January, feels like “a weird kind of homecoming.” Over coffee at Thessaloniki’s Mediterranean Palace, the 30-year-old still seems awestruck by her meteoric rise. Just over two months ago, Arcel was herself a relative unknown, with a career that had mostly spanned the stage and television. Before her Venice breakout, her only appearances on the big screen were in supporting roles. After accepting best actress honors on the Lido, Arcel revealed to Danish media that she’d been collecting unemployment benefits ahead of the Italian fest; she was on her way to report to a job center in Copenhagen when she got word that she needed to fly back to Venice for the award ceremony. articles.title: ‘Dhurandhar,’ ‘Kantara: A Legend – Chapter 1’ Among Indian Panorama Lineup at IFFI Goa
articles.content: Aditya Dhar’s Hindi-language “ Dhurandhar ” will open the Indian Panorama section of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa. Rishab Shetty’s Kannada-language “Kantara: A Legend – Chapter 1” is also in the lineup. Leena Yadav’s “Becoming,” in Ladakhi, will kick off the non-feature program. In all, IFFI’s annual survey of Indian filmmaking will present 25 features and 20 non-features this year. Related Stories 'Adults' Renewed for Season 3 at FX “Dhurandhar” and “Kantara: A Legend – Chapter 1” both sit in the five-title Mainstream Cinema strand. A 12-member jury chaired by Indian National Film Award-winning filmmaker Madhur Bhandarkar picked the features from 404 submissions. The other 20 titles cover 12 languages, from Hindi, Tamil and Bengali to Tulu and Nyishi. articles.title: Jakarta World Cinema Expands to Malang and Bandung, Where Palme d’Or Winner ‘Fjord’ Opens Festival
articles.content: Jakarta World Cinema has taken its festival outside the Indonesian capital for the first time, with the inaugural Bandung World Cinema and Malang World Cinema opening simultaneously on Nov. 14 in two cities with large student populations and busy creative scenes. Bandung’s screenings are taking place at CGV Paris Van Java, while Malang’s are at Cinépolis Malang Town Square, with both editions running through Nov. 21. The move takes the festival to audiences who have tracked the Jakarta event from elsewhere in the country. Related Stories 'Adults' Renewed for Season 3 at FX The Bandung edition is programming 203 international titles drawn from 69 countries. Cristian Mungiu’s “ Fjord ,” which won this year’s Palme d’Or at Cannes, opened proceedings. Also on the slate are Beth de Araujo’s “Josephine,” which took both the Grand Jury Prize and the Audience Award in Sundance’s U.S. Dramatic Competition in 2026, and Marine Atlan’s “La Gradiva,” winner of the AMI Paris Grand Prize at this year’s Cannes Critics’ Week. Sandra Wollner’s “Everytime,” which picked up the Un Certain Regard Prize at Cannes, screens alongside Kurosawa Kiyoshi’s new feature “The Samurai and the Prisoner,” a Cannes Premiere selection. The festival’s online program, available until Nov. 21, includes Ildiko Enyedi’s “Silent Friend,” a Fipresci Prize winner at Venice in 2025, and Ilker Çatak’s “Yellow Letters,” this year’s Golden Bear winner at the Berlinale. “Bandung World Cinema gives the local audience an unprecedented opportunity to watch alternative cinema outside of the mainstream Hollywood films that dominate the theaters. articles.title: Hoobastank, Simple Plan and More Bands Performed Mid-Flight During Nationwide Air Travel Ground Stop
articles.content: Southwest Airlines brought back its “Live at 35” program during Friday’s nationwide grounding of air travel with performances from artists on their way to Vans Warped Tour . Hoobastank , The Used, Simple Plan and Lolo performed aboard a Southwest flight from Los Angeles to Orlando, Fla., on Nov. 13 as part of the music program, which hosts surprise midflight pop-up performances. The flight left Los Angeles around 11 a.m., about two hours before the FAA declared a national ground stop that snarled global travel and left more than 1 million people stranded. Related Stories 'Adults' Renewed for Season 3 at FX Hoobastank took to the aisles at cruising altitude for a live rendition of their 2004 hit “The Reason.” Passengers sang along and posted about the performance on social media. Lolo, who played at Warped Tour’s Long Beach, Calif., stop in July, wrote “Every plane was grounded today, but the emo gods made sure this one flew.” The sky-high performance came amid a nationwide ground stop for all flights, with the Federal Aviation Administration citing “extraordinary circumstances.” The initial alert came just after 1 p.m. PT on Friday, stranding some 1.5 million travelers by CNN’s estimate. Airborne flights were allowed to continue, but new domestic flights were delayed or canceled, throwing travel plans into question for various industry events over the weekend. The stop was lifted about five hours later, shortly before 6 p.m. PT. The “Live at 35” artists were in route to the final Vans Warped Tour 2026 stop in Orlando, which runs Nov. 14-15 at Camping World Stadium Campus. The Warped Tour expanded from three to five locations in 2026, with two-day festivals in Washington, D.C., Long Beach and Orlando, Fla. alongside two new international sites in Montreal and Mexico City. articles.title: Phil Collins Says He's a 'Well Man' Now and Hints at the 'Possibility of Doing Some Shows' Amid Health Battle: ‘You Haven’t Heard the Last of Me…
articles.content: Phil Collins made a rare public appearance to accept his induction into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame at the ceremony in Los Angeles on Saturday, where he addressed his health, calling himself “a well man now.” “Thank you so much. Thank you. I’m really not as bad as it looks. I’m much better,” Collins said at the beginning of his speech. “I’ve got to say, there are lots of rumors about whether I’m going to sing, do a tour of an album, but you haven’t heard the last of me,” he added. Related Stories 'Adults' Renewed for Season 3 at FX In the press room after the ceremony, he explained that he has an in-house recording studio and a band of fellow musicians that make it possible — and even enjoyable — for him to keep making music. He hopes to share this music and tour down the road. “Everything started to go wrong,” the musician said. “So at one point I didn’t think I’d live, let alone go on the road again. But just the other night I was talking to the kids about it, and everyone got excited, including myself, that it’s not beyond the realm of possibility of doing some shows.” “I’ve got some great friends of mine that are great musicians that have been in my band. And I’d like to get down to my studio just to have some fun and write some music that I hope will be good enough for people to hear and sort of enjoy,” he added. “So it’s a work in progress.” Collins has often been open about his health issues. He told The Times of London in August that he almost died in 2024 from health complications stemming from alcohol abuse. In early 2026, he told BBC Two that he’s undergone five surgeries on his knee. Despite his health challenges, he is determined to continue his music career. “Well, you say something once and you gotta answer questions about it forever. I can’t believe that I’m not going to do something. I’m not very good at doing nothing,” Collins told reporters.

articles.title: Phoebe Bridgers’ Skeletal Transformation on ‘SNL’ Wasn’t Just a Startling Special Effect — It Emotionally Elevated One of the Best Pop Songs Ever…
articles.content: On her first appearance as a solo artist on “ Saturday Night Live ” since 2021. Phoebe Bridgers didn’t break any guitars this time. But maybe some hearts. Or perhaps the impact was felt more as a chill down the spine. However it was received, Bridgers’ performance of “Still Standing” turned out to be a spooky stunner, pairing her already personal and emotional lyrics with the coup de grace no one saw coming: her face’s sudden transformation into a skull. If this were any halfway-standard “ SNL ” musical number, the visually shocking special might have seemed like a belated Halloween stunt. But “Still Standing” is an extraordinary piece of work, focused, as any serious fan well knows, on her father’s death. So at a key moment near the end of the solo acosutic performance, the abrupt transition gave an extra jolt of life, so to speak, to one of the best modern pop songs ever written about death and how we process it. On the most mundane (but still fascinating level), there’s the question of how they pulled it off. It was a practical effect, and not a digital one. Bridgers was wearing UV-sensitive skull makeup under her other makeup for her entire time on “SNL,” including her preceding number. The changeover almost felt like a jump cut, but it was black lights making the hidden skull come alive. It was spooky, but spooky with a point: Without trying to put too definite a meaning on it, it was as if Bridgers was having to go over to the other side, herself, to figure out how to grapple with a semi-estranged family member’s passing and legacy, since trying to get that right on this side of the veil is a pretty effed-up mess. Besides “Still Standing” having been a widely picked-over standout track on her recent “Lost Weekend” album, it’s been at the forefront of many fans’ minds because of the central place it has on the “Lost” tour that just swung through U.S. arenas. articles.title: ‘The Gilded Age’ Star Denée Benton on Peggy’s Big Day: “It Was Like Eating Candy and Steak All at the Same Time”
articles.content: SPOILER ALERT: The following story contains plot details from “Ain’t That Good News,” Season 4, Episode 3 of “ The Gilded Age ,” now streaming on HBO Max. “That’s always been the really long game, intentional pursuit that I’ve been on with the show,” says Denée Benton, the actor who portrays the enterprising secretary turned journalist turned novelist — and now, bride! — on HBO’s “The Gilded Age.” In an accurate reflection of the 19th century, Peggy has been handed some of the heaviest material on Julian Fellowes’ hit period drama. But Benton has also advocated for her character to partake in some of the lush fantasy that otherwise pervades the show. And starting with last season’s meet-cute with handsome doctor William Kirkland (Jordan Donica), Peggy did. This Sunday, Peggy and William’s romance reached its zenith with the couple’s wedding, one of the most emotional and cathartic scenes “The Gilded Age” has produced to date. Benton namechecks Emmy-winning production designer Bob Shaw, costume designer Kasia Walicka-Maimone and producing director Salli Richardson Whitfield with bringing Peggy’s walk down the aisle to life. “They did us such justice with how stunning it all looks. The amount of background that it took to fill that church, and to shoot in a church from that time with the stained Tiffany glass and the light shining in — it made the whole room have this warm glow.” Peggy and William’s nuptials aren’t just a hard-won moment for the couple themselves. As written by Fellowes and executive producer Sonja Warfield, who share credit on the season’s scripts, the wedding is loaded with the significance of a Black couple forming a family just a couple of decades after the Civil War. (Both of Peggy’s parents are formerly enslaved.) articles.title: ‘Slow Horses’ Will End With Season 8, Says Olivia Cooke: ‘We’re All Melancholy… The Show’s Been a Shining Light’
articles.content: Bad news for “ Slow Horses ” fans: star Olivia Cooke recently told The Times that the eighth season will be the show’s last. “I am shooting the last season!” she said, before adding: “Never say never!” Cooke continues: “But I think that’s what we’ve been told and it definitely feels like we are ending. We’re all melancholy, distracted. Yesterday, I got in the make-up chair and cried. The show’s been a shining light and I’ve told my partner I need two weeks to get over it. I’m going to be depressed.” Related Stories 'Adults' Renewed for Season 3 at FX Cooke originated the role of Sid Baker in the show’s first season, before being seemingly killed off. She reprised the role in Season 6, very much still alive in the show’s universe. The actress tells The Times that she wasn’t surprised to return , as “they were checking my availability over the years. And we stayed in touch. It was like I’d never left.” Cooke revealed that her role on HBO’s “House of the Dragon” had made a return to the show complicated in past seasons. “There was something in my contract for ‘House of the Dragon’ which said I was not allowed to do a long-running series for an opposing streamer, so we had to smooth that out,” she said, noting lawyers got involved. “I sent texts saying, ‘Help!’” “Slow Horses” was renewed by Apple for Season 8 back in September ahead of the premiere of Season 6. articles.content: Russell Brand and his wife, Laura Gallacher, have spoken about the actor’s 10-year and six-month prison sentence after being convicted of rape and sexual assault following his London criminal trial earlier this month. The couple shared remarks in a YouTube video posted Sunday, in which Gallacher speaks about the conviction before continuing to the pre-recorded episode of their “Sunday Service with the Brands” series, which featured Brand, and concluded by reading a message from her husband. articles.title: John Mulaney Mocks Robert F. Kennedy Jr. in ‘SNL’ Monologue: ‘No One Likes Him. You Dumbass … Your Thing Can’t Be the Measles!’
articles.content: John Mulaney ‘s opening monologue on this week’s “ Saturday Night Live ” took an unexpected turn when he mocked controversial U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services Robert F. Kennedy Jr. The comic started by impersonating Kennedy, saying, “‘My father was a good man, and I’m a lousy man, but I have the same name. Am I good if I have the same name as my father? No, please, let me be in charge of your bones and your tummy. Please allow me to control how your blood feels in your butt and everywhere. Stop the science … Robitussin, when taken during menstruation, will cause telekinesis. This is clear from the pamphlets in my rental car.’” Related Stories 'Adults' Renewed for Season 3 at FX Mulaney then slammed Kennedy’s vaccine skepticism, saying, “No one likes him. You dumbass … your thing can’t be the measles!” He then mocked Kennedy’s previous occupation as an environmental lawyer, saying, “He would just join cases late if they were about to be successful. ‘Are you about to win? I’m part of this too.’” Mulaney then described how he interacted with the politician by performing comedy at benefits for Kennedy’s Riverkeepers organization. “They were in charge of keeping the Hudson River in New York City clean,” Mulaney said. “That was his job. That’s how good he is at jobs. His old job was keeping the Hudson River, whose native fish are tied-off used condoms, clean. Now he’s in charge of all of our tummies.” The Nov. 14 episode was Mulaney’s seventh as host. His monologue also touched on family issues and children whose deep, scratchy voices remind him of Kennedy.

The contest was aired in the participating countries as well as on Eurovision’s official YouTube channel. EBU members TVP (Poland), Sveriges Radio (Sweden), Kan (Israel) and SBS (Australia) also broadcast the contest, which was hosted by Thai TV stars Woody Milintachinda and Cindy Bishop. As well as the competing countries, Thai superstar Jeff Satur performed alongside this year’s Eurovision winner Dara , who took first place for Bulgaria in the May contest with her track “Bangaranga.” The show, which also included a special opening performance celebrating the host city, was produced by Voxovation and Bangkok-based S20 Productions. articles.title: Dawn Greenhalgh, Canadian Stage Veteran Who Voiced the Queen in ‘Babar,’ Dies at 93
articles.content: Dawn Greenhalgh, a veteran Canadian actress of stage, film and television, died Nov. 6 in Toronto. She was 93. Born in Shanghai, China, she spent her childhood with her family in a Japanese prisoner of war camp, where she discovered a love for music, theater and dance. Greenhalgh moved to Canada with only a guardian at the age of 14, attending Montreal High School and beginning her performing career. Related Stories 'Adults' Renewed for Season 3 at FX In 1953, at 19 years old, she became a founding member of Canada’s Stratford Festival. She went on to become a founding member of the Neptune Theatre in Halifax and Theatre Plus in Toronto. She performed on stages around the world and in New York studied with Uta Haagen, Herbert Berghof and Mira Rostova. Greenhalgh’s film roles included Sofia Coppola ‘s “The Virgin Suicides” and David Cronenberg’s “Map to the Stars.” She also worked with her daughter, Megan Follows, in the popular Canadian series “Anne of Green Gables.” Other television appearances included “Five Days at Memorial,” “Saving Hope” and “La Femme Nikita.” She voiced Queen Celeste, Babar the elephant’s wife, on the animated series “Babar.” With the Stratford Festival, she performed in plays including “All’s Well That Ends Well” with Alec Guinness, “Antony and Cleopatra” and “Love’s Labour’s Lost.” “Dawn Greenhalgh was a powerhouse, a dynamic, brilliant actress,” Stratford Festival Artistic Director Antoni Cimolino wrote on Instagram . “As an extraordinary artist she could be both charming and unsettling. It was a pleasure to hear her perspective on plays and productions as it was informed by a lifetime of wide experience, a sparkling intellect and an independent, free thinking mind.” She is survived by her children Edwina Follows; Laurence Follows; Samantha Follows and Megan Follows, six grandchildren and two step-grandchildren.

articles.title: ‘The Good Daughter’ Stars Rose Byrne and Meghann Fahy on Playing Sisters With Secrets and That Twisty Killer Ending
articles.content: SPOILER ALERT: This interview contains major spoilers from “ The Good Daughter ,” now streaming on Peacock. For Sam and Charlie Quinn, the estranged sisters played by Rose Byrne and Meghann Fahy in “The Good Daughter,” the truth was always going to set them free. Adapted by author Karin Slaughter from her own bestselling novel of the same name, the six-episode Peacock series gradually unravels a Southern Gothic family mystery. More than 20 years earlier, two masked gunmen broke into the Quinns’ rural Georgia home, murdering their mother, Gamma (Olivia Williams), and leaving both sisters with life-altering injuries. Rather than bonding them, the tragedy and a subsequent web of secrets drove the girls apart, culminating in a bitter falling-out a decade ago despite their shared career path. While Sam built a lucrative career in patent law in New York City, Charlie followed in her father Rusty’s (Brendan Gleeson) footsteps to practice criminal defense law in their shady fictional hometown of Pikeville. But when Charlie witnesses a tragic school shooting that leaves principal Douglas Pinkman (Kovar McClure) and a young student dead, Sam is pulled back to her old stomping grounds after Rusty is badly injured taking the suspect’s case. articles.content: Actor Skip Hinnant , best known for his work on the PBS children’s series “ The Electric Company ‘ and as the voice of Fritz the Cat in Ralph Bakshi’s racy animated films from the 1970s, has died. He was 86. Hinnant’s death was confirmed by his family in an obituary notice published by the New York Times. He died Nov. 8 in Denver. Hinnant was active in theater in the 1960s. He originated the role of Schroeder in the Off Broadway debut of Peanuts musical “You’re a Good Man, Charlie Brown” in 1967. He was part of the renowned Julius Monk revue “Struts and Frets” in 1963. The previous year, Hinnant had a recurring role on the popular ABC sitcom “The Patty Duke Show.” He appeared at the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner in 1962, performing for President John F. He was also known for his active involvement with Actors Equity, AFTRA and SAG (before the latter unions merged) from the 1980s through the early 2000s. Born Joseph Howard Hinnant in 1940, he grew up in Chincoteague Island, Virginia. He was nicknamed Skip by his older sister Jean. The name stuck as his acting career blossomed. articles.content: China celebrated its Golden Rooster Awards this past Tuesday night in a glittering ceremony hosted inside the palatial Xiamen Strait Grand Theater in Xiamen, Fujian Province, China. The southern seaside city hosted generations of stars — from current hotshot Jackson Yee ( Resurrection ) to acclaimed auteur Zhang Yimou — for an event that is the highlight of the annual state-run Golden Rooster and Hundred Flowers Film Festival. Hong Kong’s Tony Leung Ka Fai stole the show, winning his first Golden Rooster best actor nod for his turn as the villain in the Larry Yang-directed thriller The Shadow’s Edge — some 25 years on from sending hearts a flutter across the globe in Jean-Jacques Annaud’s steamy The Lover . articles.summary: “Not to defend 'SNL,' they don’t approve it. I mean, they could shut it down. They could, but you don’t write your set and give it to them. Unless you’re not a comedian," he said on a podcast.
articles.content: Shane Gillis is finally addressing his controversial Saturday Night Live monologue. During the Oct. 10 episode of the NBC sketch comedy series, Gillis, who hosted the show, accused women of “dressing like whores” at the gym during his opening monologue. The joke drew backlash from audiences and fellow comedians. On a Friday episode of the Joe Rogan Experience , Gillis explained that SNL didn’t give him feedback on the material beforehand. “Not to defend SNL, they don’t approve it. I mean, they could shut it down. They could, but you don’t write your set and give it to them. Unless you’re not a comedian,” he said. “I’m sure non-comics, they write the set for them. They have writers that write the monologue for them.” Related Stories TV Bowen Yang Makes Surprise 'SNL' Appearance as Jensen Huang as John Mulaney Pokes at FAA Ground Stop and Microsoft Outage in Cold Open TV TV Ratings: 'SNL' Hits Two-Year High With Druski as Host “The funniest part was, they were like, ‘What’s going on with the monologue?’ And I was like, ‘It’s not great, but I don’t say anything bad,'” Gillis continued. “The whole time, I was like, ‘Fellas, I’m giving you a solid C minus of a monologue, but I promise there’s no controversy. I’m calling myself fat for fucking 10 minutes. That’s it.'” Gillis said he thinks the backlash “obviously had a lot to do with the climate.” The monologue drew criticism from Dan Levy , former SNL castmember Ego Nwodim and Obsession star Inde Navarrette , who took a dig at the joke during her opening monologue on the show’s Halloween episode. Meanwhile, others came to the comedian’s defense , including David Spade, Dana Carvey and Jimmy Carr. In 2019, Gillis was announced as a new SNL castmember but was fired before making his debut after past podcast comments resurfaced .

articles.summary: He also played Cathy’s boyfriend on ‘The Patty Duke Show’ and Schroeder on the stage in ‘You’re a Good Man, Charlie Brown.’
articles.content: Skip Hinnant, who portrayed the wordsmith Fargo North, Decoder and other characters as an original castmember on The Electric Company and voiced the hedonistic Fritz the Cat in a pair of animated movies, has died. He was 86. Hinnant started his career with a recurring role as Ted, boyfriend to Patty’s identical twin sister, Cathy, on the first two seasons of ABC’s The Patty Duke Show from 1963-65. While on the kids show, Hinnant went in another direction by voicing the leftist, perpetually stoned title feline in Fritz the Cat (1972), based on the comic strip by Robert Crumb and directed by Ralph Bakshi. Guthrie, the popular co-anchor of NBC’s Today show, has been the news as much as she’s reported the news this year. In the early morning hours of Feb. 1, 2026, Guthrie’s mom Nancy Guthrie was kidnapped from her Tucson, Arizona home. Nancy Guthrie is presumed dead though her remains have never been found. Nancy was 84 years old and in poor health. She did not have her necessary medication with her. Related Stories TV The Other Midterms Flip: Broadcast Networks, Led by NBC, Dominated Election Night Coverage TV Carson Daly Named Co-Anchor of NBC's 'Saturday Today' On Feb. 10, doorbell footage of a masked man approaching her home on the night of her disappearance was made public. No suspect was ever identified. A pair of notes from the purported kidnapper(s) were sent to local news outlets. The first demanded Bitcoin for Nancy’s safe return; the second note did not demand money but stated that Nancy died shortly after her abduction. The second note reads, in full: “Guthrie Family, We did not fully grasp the seriousness of her physical condition. We never intended to hurt her, that was not our intention. She perished shortly after she was taken. We believe it was heart related. She is buried in nature now. Nothing you could have done could have changed the outcome. We want your family to know this and hope you can all find peace. We are truly sorry.” Savannah Guthrie returned to work at the NBC morning show in April. Craig Melvin is her Today show co-anchor. Guthrie is set to co-host the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade with her usual collaborators Hoda Kotb and Al Roker. This Thanksgiving marks the 100th anniversary of the procession. The Macy’s march actually began in 1924, but it took a three-year hiatus during World War II.

articles.title: Streaming Ratings: ‘From’ Dominates an Otherwise Quiet Halloween Week
articles.summary: The sci-fi/horror series is the only title to draw more than a billion minutes of watch time.
articles.content: The last week of October was a relatively quiet one on Nielsen’s streaming charts, with one big exception. From , the MGM+ show that was added to Netflix’s library on Oct. 19, spent its second straight week as the No. 1 overall title. The series drew 2.04 billion minutes of watch time, up 24 percent week to week . From also surpassed the mark it set a week earlier for the most viewing minutes for an acquired series this year. Beyond From , however, there weren’t a lot of highlights. No other series or movie cracked the billion-minute mark. The top 10 overall titles combined for 9.03 billion minutes of viewing, down from 9.22 billion the previous week. Netflix’s Nobody Wants This (847 million minutes) led the original series top 10. The comedy was up about 17 percent week to week but once again trailed its performance from a year ago. In the two weeks after season three’s Oct. 22 premiere, Nobody Wants This has totaled 1.57 billion viewing minutes, off about 14 percent from 1.83 billion minutes for the same time frame after season two’s debut last year. Love Is Blind (796 million minutes), VisionQuest (548 million) and Tulsa King (501 million) all posted small week to week improvements. Netflix’s Lupin (579 million) had the week’s best premiere, and the short docuseries The One About Matthew Perry had 541 million minutes of viewing. Hocus Pocus rose to the top of the movie rankings during Halloween week, scoring 405 million minutes of viewing on Disney+. The Nightmare Before Christmas, Coraline, Coco and Hocus Pocus 2 also made the top 10. Nielsen’s streaming ratings cover viewing on TV sets only and don’t include minutes watched on computers or mobile devices. The ratings only measure U.S. audiences. articles.summary: He and his identical twin, Joseph, shared roles as Bobby Ewing on the CBS show and as Penelope Ann Miller’s son in the Arnold Schwarzenegger movie.
articles.content: Christian Cousins, who with his identical twin brother shared roles as youngsters on the CBS primetime soap Knots Landing and in the Arnold Schwarzenegger film Kindergarten Cop , has died. He was 43. Cousins died Oct. 20 after a battle with liver disease, his half-brother Jonas Roeser announced on Instagram. “He was a character, full of passion and energy, with big stories and even bigger dreams,” he wrote. articles.title: ‘Downstate’ Broadway Review: Bruce Norris Proves Again That He’s a Great Playwright
articles.summary: The most unlikely subject matter for a show on Broadway proves exactly why it belongs there The post ‘Downstate’ Broadway Review: Bruce Norris Proves Again That He’s a Great Playwright appeared first on TheWrap .
articles.content: The most unlikely subject matter for a show on Broadway proves exactly why it belongs there For a Broadway audience, playwright Bruce Norris could have weighted the theatrical playing field slightly more. He could have written a play about a recovery house for MAGA Republicans. Instead, he has written a play about child sex offenders. Norris’ play “Downstate” opened Sunday at Booth Theatre after productions at Off Broadway’s Playwrights Horizons, Chicago’s Steppenwolf and London’s National Theatre. “Downstate” takes place in a church-run residence for sex offenders who live in a house that is continually being vandalized. Those concerned (and often violent) neighbors have also joined forces to expand the safety-zone perimeter around a local school that will have the effect of restricting even further the mobility, not to mention the grocery-shopping habits, of these four men convicted of sex crimes against minors. The warning about the new law comes courtesy of Ivy (Liza Colon-Zayas), a case worker who shows little sympathy for her charges. She’s just one woman against four men, but Ivy has the law on her side and wears it like an AR-45 bulletproof body armor. Norris also uses Ivy’s status in the legal system to toy with our sympathies. As precise as a metronome, this playwright’s exposition drops one fact after another regarding just how little freedom these men retain after serving considerable prison sentences. No cellphones, no internet access, no credit cards, no female visitors, no alcohol — the list is itemized, each restriction methodically spaced and delivered throughout the two hours and 30 minutes of this two-act play. Somewhere in the second act, the police monitor wrapped around their ankles becomes the least of these men’s problems. Act 1 hits an early climax when Ivy sits down to talk with one of those sex offenders. articles.content: The Marvel Studios chief reflects on bringing the original mutant stars into the MCU for “Avengers: Doomsday” Kevin Feige is bringing Marvel’s cinematic history full circle with “Avengers: Doomsday,” and the Marvel Studios president says reuniting the original X-Men with Earth’s Mightiest Heroes was a fitting way to mark the occasion. In a new interview with Empire , Feige explained why bringing the mutant superheroes into the “Avengers” franchise felt like the right move, particularly given his connection with the original “X-Men” films. It’s a connection that dates back to 2000’s “X-Men,” on which Feige served as an associate producer. Released nearly a decade before the Marvel Cinematic Universe officially began with 2008’s “Iron Man,” the film helped establish the modern superhero blockbuster era and introduced audiences to a live-action version of Marvel’s mutant team. The franchise would go on to produce 14 live-action movies, that include spin-offs like “Deadpool.” “You see interviews of Hugh Jackman 15, 20 years ago saying, ‘People say it’s impossible, but maybe someday the X-Men and the Avengers can all get together,” Feige told the publication. “It just felt right. It just felt like the fun way to culminate a quarter-century of storytelling.” While “X-Men” and Marvel fans had long hoped to see the characters cross over on screen, as they frequently do in the comics, that possibility only became a reality in 2019, after Disney acquired 20th Century Fox, which had previously held the film rights to the mutant superheroes. So now, more than 25 years later, several familiar faces from that original franchise are finally joining the MCU’s expanding ensemble in “Avengers: Doomsday.” Patrick Stewart (in his final film performance), Ian McKellen, Rebecca Romijn, James Marsden, Alan Cumming and Kelsey Grammer are among the actors reprising their respective roles as Professor X, Magneto, Mystique, Cyclops, Nightcrawler and Beast. articles.title: Sean Duffy Says ‘I Don’t Apologize’ for Friday’s Nationwide Ground Stop
articles.summary: The transportation secretary argues that decades of underinvestment has left the nation's air traffic control system in need of a major overhaul The post Sean Duffy Says ‘I Don’t Apologize’ for Friday’s Nationwide Ground Stop appeared first on TheWrap .
articles.content: The transportation secretary argues that decades of underinvestment has left the nation’s air traffic control system in need of a major overhaul Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Sunday he could not apologize for the decades-old air traffic control infrastructure that contributed to Friday’s nationwide ground stop , arguing that years of underinvestment by both political parties left the Trump administration with a system in need of major repairs. Appearing on NBC’s “Meet the Press,” Duffy defended the administration’s response to Friday’s disruption, which grounded flights across the country, and pushed back when asked whether he owed the American people an apology because the problems had occurred on his watch. The news show’s moderator Kristen Welker noted that FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford had apologized to the American people during a news conference Saturday and asked Duffy whether he felt he owed an apology as transportation secretary. “I can’t apologize for what was passed off to us,” Duffy responded. “And I can’t blame Republicans or Democrats because it’s all of them. It goes back, 20, 25, 30 years of a lack of investment.” Duffy also said he was moving faster than previous administrations to address the problems at the Federal Aviation Administration and Department of Transportation, crediting President Donald Trump with securing $12.5 billion for aviation modernization through the One Big Beautiful Bill. However, he argued that the funding was insufficient to complete the overhaul, saying Congress had restricted how the money could be spent and had not allocated enough for telecommunications and new software. Duffy said the administration expected to spend the $12.5 billion by the end of 2028 but needed additional funding to build a more resilient telecommunications architecture and modernize the system’s software. articles.content: Mia Latter, previously identified as “Alice,” alleges Brand raped her when she was 16 and is speaking publicly to push for legal protections for teenagers Mia Latter, a woman who previously accused Russell Brand of sexual abuse when she was a teenager, has waived her right to lifelong anonymity and is speaking publicly about her allegations against the actor-comedian as she campaigns for changes to the United Kingdom’s age of consent laws. Latter, now 37, alleged that Brand orally raped her when she was 16 and he was 30. She had previously been identified only as “Alice” in a 2023 investigation by The Times , The Sunday Times and Channel 4’s “Dispatches,” which examined allegations of sexual misconduct by Brand. In an interview with The Sunday Times , Latter said she wants the U.K. to introduce a staggered age of consent that would prohibit adults from having sexual relationships with 16- and 17-year-olds. The country’s current age of consent is 16, regardless of the age of the other person, although additional legal protections apply to minors. Latter said she decided to make her identity public in the hope that her experience could help protect other teenagers from grooming and exploitation. She alleged that she first encountered Brand in 2006 in London’s Leicester Square while returning home after doing some shopping. Brand, who was working for MTV at the time, approached her, took her phone number and later contacted her about going to dinner. Latter said she disclosed that she was 16 before they began seeing each other, but he continued pursuing the relationship. According to Latter, Brand subsequently instructed her to keep their relationship a secret, although members of his entourage were aware of it. When the “28 Years Later” trilogy was first announced, Boyle, Garland, and Sony’s Columbia Pictures planned to film the first two installments back-to-back, with Nia DaCosta directing “The Bone Temple.” “The overall arc is outlined, but we’ve got to raise the money first. articles.content: Jordan Firstman’s “ Club Kid ” was the belle of Cannes. Critics raved about Firstman’s feature directorial debut, as well as his sensitive performance as a party promoter turned unlikely dad, and A24 swept in to buy the film for $17 million after a bidding war. But plenty of movies have been embraced at film festivals only to face rejection when they hit the wider world. Would “Club Kid” be another “Dope” or “Begin Again”? Well, based on a very limited sample size, “Club Kid” seems to be performing just fine, thank you very much. Those raves and A24’s imprimatur of cool are paying off as the film enjoyed the best limited expansion of the year this weekend, grossing $756,060 across 27 screens. That translates into an impressive $28,002 per-screen average. Since opening in six screens on Nov. 6, “Club Kid” has earned nearly $1.5 million. But this very New York story has mostly played in major cities and liberal bastions like the Big Apple, Chicago, Austin, San Francisco, and Los Angeles. Will audiences across the country embrace the story of a drug-taking, sex-positive gay man and his adorable 10-year-old accidental son? We’ll find out on Thanksgiving when it goes wide. articles.content: If Johnny Depp was hoping that “ Ebenezer ” would mark a glorious return to mainstream movies, he may need to hold out for another vehicle. But over the course of nearly two decades behind the camera, Feste has carved out a particular sweet spot, regardless of the genre or the cast or the wider world her stories fit inside: She likes complicated women. Not unlikable women, but messy women, contradictory women, women who get things done their own way. This year alone, his work includes “The Invite” with director and actor Olivia Wilde, as well as teaming up with Jordan Firstman on A24’s “ Club Kid, ” in which Firstman directs and stars. Newport-Berra ( Variety’s 10 Artisans to Watch 2026 ) says, “I tend to enjoy working with actor-directors because we get this dynamic experience on set where they get to direct the film both from outside and from within during the scene, which I think is a special opportunity for a director to be able to be inside the scene, guiding it as it’s happening.” Related Stories 'Adults' Renewed for Season 3 at FX While “The Invite” challenged him to work with Wilde to be creative within a single space, “Club Kid” — which opens this weekend — is set in New York City. The film stars Firstman, Cara Delevingne, Diego Calva, Kirby Howell-Baptiste and Reggie Absolom. It follows a queer party promoter who has long outgrown his time on the scene.
